copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Tuesday, late-night UTC kickoff, brings Iraq and Norway together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Iraq side, by +10.3pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

Elo numbers going in: Iraq 1540, Norway 1760. That's a 220-point lead for Norway — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Iraq to win at 18%, the draw at 17%, and Norway to win at 65%. The home side reads 18% on this distribution — the model's central case for Iraq.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Iraq to win at 8%, the draw at 15%, and Norway to win at 78%. The Iraq side trades at 8% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +1150. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 18%, +10.3pp wider.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Iraq the lower bound is 14%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +5.9pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 28 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Iraq a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +10.3pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The market reads Iraq as a 8% chance; our Elo prior reads them at 18%. A +10.3pp gap on a longshot side is where the engine finds its biggest Picks.
copy.title: Iraq v Norway · the model leans Iraq
